_note: A LapEE running as a tunnel broker that charges for the traffic it carries, and publishes a location record so it can be found. Replace the signers, the device pins, the ledger address and location-url with your own.
_note-rates: metering@1.0 sizes the bodies P4 gives it: request-bytes is what arrives, response-bytes is what the node returns. A tunnelled node POSTs its payload to the broker, so the traffic a tunnel serves to the public arrives here as a REQUEST. Selling egress therefore means pricing request-bytes.
_note-price: 1 base unit per byte, roughly $2/TB: an AO token is 1e12 base units and trades around $2. Sizes are of the ETF encoding, not wire octets, so calibrate against observed traffic.
_note-ledger: Seed each node allowed to rent a tunnel. 1e12 base units is 1 AO, about 1 TB of egress at the rate above. Seed generously while testing: a 402 writes the negative balance before testing it and never reverses it, and requeued deliveries re-charge per dispatch.
_note-location: The location@1.0 start hook publishes a signed record naming this node's public URL, which is how clients discover it. location-url is published verbatim and permanently; left unset it is built from node_host and port and claims http://localhost:8734. init prepends this hook to the enforced measurement and zone hooks, so both still run and measurement still measures the final node.
_note-hooks: p4@1.0 must precede tunnel@1.0 in on/request: p4 opens the metering session in the request hook and prices it in the response hook, and metering@1.0 measures between the two. Reverse the order and nothing is priced.
